title: Vitamin D Supplements for Prevention of Tuberculosis Infection and Disease
authors: Ganmaa D, Uyanga B, Zhou X, Gantsetseg G, Delgerekh B, Enkhmaa D, et al.
population: Schoolchildren aged 6 to 13 years in 18 public schools of Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, with a negative QuantiFERON-TB Gold In-Tube result; mean baseline 25-hydroxyvitamin D 11.9 ng/ml, 95.6% below 20 ng/ml and 31.8% below 10 ng/ml
funder: Supported by an award (1R01HL122624-01) from the National Institutes of Health. The author manuscript read contains no statement on the role of the funder.
authorConflicts: Disclosure forms available with the full text at NEJM.org; not read.
result: Weekly vitamin D3 14,000 IU (n=4418) against placebo (n=4433) for 3 years: positive QuantiFERON result 147 of 4074 (3.6%) against 134 of 4043 (3.3%), adjusted RR 1.10 (95% CI 0.87 to 1.38); tuberculosis disease 21 of 4401 against 25 of 4418, RR 0.87 (0.49 to 1.55); hospitalisation for acute respiratory infection 29 against 34, RR 0.86 (0.52 to 1.40). End-of-trial 25-hydroxyvitamin D 31.0 against 10.7 ng/ml. Deaths 4 against 6; one child in the vitamin D group developed symptomatic hypercalcaemia (corrected calcium 2.70 mmol/L), which resolved after vitamin D was stopped; three children had 25-hydroxyvitamin D above 80 ng/ml at 3 years without symptoms.
